html:
The Gunaikurnai, or Kurnai, are an Aboriginal Australian nation of southeast Australia. They are the Traditional Custodians of most of Gippsland in eastern Victoria and much of the southern slopes of the Victorian Alps. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

The nation is made up of five major clans. Their country includes the Gippsland Lakes, a chain of coastal lagoons behind a long sand barrier, where fish, eels and waterbirds were plentiful, and forests and high plains inland.

Squatters came into Gippsland from the late 1830s and early 1840s, led in part by the Scottish explorer Angus McMillan. The Kurnai resisted, and a string of massacres followed, among them Warrigal Creek in 1843, one of the deadliest in Victoria's history. Many survivors were later gathered on the Lake Tyers and Ramahyuck missions. Neighbours on the map include the Bidhawal, the Jaitmatang and the Boonwurrung. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
